sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: A baobab native to northern Madagascar, especially the far north around Antsiranana. A recent peer-reviewed study describes trees up to about 25 m tall and 2–5 m in trunk diameter, with a characteristically horizontal, T- or Y-shaped crown. Edible use was not verified.

sections.title: Conservation and comparison
sections.text: Kew reports the IUCN status as Endangered. This species shares northern Madagascar and the genus Adansonia with A. perrieri, which Kew lists as Critically Endangered; do not transfer measurements or other traits between the species.
